words.gloss: not opposed to Vāta and Kapha
words.gram: n. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: शमी का फल गुरु, उष्ण, मधुर, रूक्ष और केशों का नाश करने वाला है। करञ्ज का (फल) विष्टम्भ करता है और वात तथा श्लेष्मा का अविरोधी है।
english: The fruit of śamī is heavy, hot, sweet, dry (rūkṣa) and destroys hair. That of karañja causes obstruction (viṣṭambha) and is not opposed to Vāta and Kapha (śleṣman).
notes: kārañja is a derived adjective 'of karañja'; 'fruit' (phala) is understood from the first line. avirodhin 'not opposed to' is kept literal (it may mean that it does not aggravate, or that it is not antagonistic to, Vāta and Kapha). viṣṭambha (obstruction, of the bowels) kept as the Sanskrit word.
lines_deva: गुरूष्णं मधुरं रूक्षं केशघ्नं च शमीफलम्
lines_iast: gurūṣṇaṃ madhuraṃ rūkṣaṃ keśaghnaṃ ca śamīphalam

hindi: आम्रातक, करमर्दक सहित अम्ल दन्तशठ, और ऐरावतक को भी रक्तपित्त करने वाला जानना चाहिए।
english: One should know āmrātaka, sour dantaśaṭha together with karamardaka, and airāvataka also, as causing raktapitta.
notes: amlam 'sour' is taken with dantaśaṭha, next to it; it may describe the whole group. The fruit names are kept in Sanskrit, no identifications. The acc. forms depend on vidyāt.

words.gram: n. acc. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: वार्ताक वात का नाश करने वाला, दीपन, कटु और तिक्त है; पर्पटकी के फल को वात बढ़ाने वाला तथा कफ और पित्त का नाश करने वाला जानना चाहिए।
english: Vārtāka destroys Vāta, stimulates digestion, and is pungent and bitter; one should know the fruit of parpaṭakī as increasing Vāta and destroying Kapha and Pitta.
notes: vārtāka = brinjal (standard). tiktaka = tikta 'bitter' with the suffix -ka.
lines_deva: वातघ्नं दीपनं चैव वार्ताकं कटु तिक्तकम्
lines_iast: vātaghnaṃ dīpanaṃ caiva vārtākaṃ kaṭu tiktakam

words.gram: n. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)
n. nom. pl., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: आक्षिकी का फल पित्त और श्लेष्मा का नाश करने वाला, अम्ल और वात बढ़ाने वाला है। (वे) मधुर, अम्ल पाक वाले और पित्त तथा श्लेष्मा को हरने वाले हैं।
english: The fruit of ākṣikī destroys Pitta and Kapha (śleṣman), is sour and increases Vāta. (They are) sweet, sour in pāka (vipāka), and remove Pitta and Kapha.
notes: SENTENCE: the neuter plural adjectives of line b have no noun inside this unit and cannot describe the singular ākṣikīphalam; the subject is supplied as '(they)'. The nearest noun is phalāni in 164a (the fruits of aśvattha, udumbara, plakṣa and nyagrodha); the predicates of 164b (astringent, sweet, sour, Vāta-increasing, heavy) do not conflict with these (sweet, sour in pāka, removing Pitta and Kapha), so line b most probably describes those fruits. pāka is taken in the sense of vipāka.

words.gloss: of aśvattha, udumbara, plakṣa and nyagrodha

hindi: और अश्वत्थ, उदुम्बर, प्लक्ष और न्यग्रोध के फल कषाय, मधुर और अम्ल, वात बढ़ाने वाले और गुरु हैं।
english: And the fruits of aśvattha, udumbara, plakṣa and nyagrodha are astringent, sweet and sour, increase Vāta and are heavy.
notes: Tree names kept in Sanskrit. 163b (n. pl., no noun of its own) most probably also describes these fruits; see 163.

words.gram: m. nom. sg., derived adj. (taddhita, from prāya-upayoga)

hindi: भल्लातक की गुठली अग्नि के समान है, उसका गूदा मधुर और शीतल है। प्रायः उपयोग में आने वाला यह पाँचवाँ फलवर्ग कहा गया।
english: The stone (asthi) of bhallātaka is like fire; its flesh is sweet and cool. This fifth group, of fruits in common use, has been stated.
notes: asthi 'bone' of a fruit = its stone; māṃsa 'flesh' of a fruit = its pulp. 'Like fire' is literal; what is fire-like (heat, burning) is not stated. svādu here as a taste = sweet.

hindi: अब हरितवर्ग — विश्वभेषज आर्द्रक रुचिकारक, दीपन और वृष्य है; वात, श्लेष्मा और विबन्ध में उसका रस बताया जाता है।
english: Now the group of greens (harita): ārdraka, the universal medicine (viśvabheṣaja), is appetizing (rocana), stimulates digestion and is aphrodisiac; its juice is advised in Vāta, Kapha (śleṣman) and constipation (vibandha).
notes: The heading 'atha haritavargaḥ' is printed on the verse line but is outside the metre (the line without it has 16 syllables). ārdraka = fresh ginger (standard); viśvabheṣaja is taken in apposition to it. vāta-śleṣma-vibandheṣu may also be read as 'in obstruction by Vāta and Kapha' (tat-puruṣa); the dvandva reading is given.
lines_deva: अथ हरितवर्गः--- रोचनं दीपनं वृष्यमार्द्रकं विश्वभेषजम्
lines_iast: atha haritavargaḥ--- rocanaṃ dīpanaṃ vṛṣyamārdrakaṃ viśvabheṣajam

words.gram: m. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: जम्बीर रुचिकारक, दीपन, तीक्ष्ण, सुगन्धित, मुख का शोधन करने वाला, कफ और वात का नाश करने वाला, कृमियों का नाश करने वाला और भोजन को पचाने वाला है।
english: Jambīra is appetizing, stimulates digestion, is sharp and fragrant, cleanses the mouth, destroys Kapha and Vāta, destroys worms (krimi) and digests food.
notes: jambīra kept in Sanskrit (an item of the greens group).

words.gram: n. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: मूलक बाल (अवस्था में) दोषों को हरने वाला है, वृद्ध (होने पर) त्रिदोष (करने वाला), स्निग्ध (द्रव्य) से सिद्ध किया हुआ मारुत को हरने वाला है; किन्तु सूखा मूलक कफ और वात को जीतने वाला है।
english: Mūlaka, when young, removes the doṣas; when mature, (it causes) the three doṣas; prepared with unctuous (substance), it removes Vāta (māruta); but dried mūlaka conquers Kapha and Vāta.
notes: mūlaka = radish (standard). tridoṣa is taken as 'causing (aggravation of) the three doṣas'. The printed commas group mārutāpaham with snigdhasiddham. snigdhasiddha may mean 'cooked with fat'; the medium is not named.

words.gloss: destroying hiccup, cough, poison, dyspnoea and pain in the sides
words.gram: m. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)
m. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: सुरस हिक्का, कास, विष, श्वास और पार्श्वशूल का नाश करने वाला, पित्त करने वाला, कफ और वात का नाश करने वाला तथा दुर्गन्ध को हरने वाला है।
english: Surasa destroys hiccup (hikkā), cough, poison, dyspnoea (śvāsa) and pain in the sides; it produces Pitta, destroys Kapha and Vāta and removes foul odour.
notes: surasa kept in Sanskrit, no identification.

hindi: यवानी, अर्जक, तथा शिग्रु, शालेय और मृष्टक हृद्य और आस्वादनीय हैं और पित्त को उत्क्लिष्ट करते हैं।
english: Yavānī, arjaka, and śigru, śāleya and mṛṣṭaka are pleasing to the heart and palatable, and stir up Pitta.

text_flags.why: grammar: there is no stem mvād; ā-√svād gives āsvādanīya 'palatable', n. nom. pl. with hṛdyāni (म्वा for स्वा, a typing slip). Metre does not object: 8 syllables either way, nyā heavy by its long vowel, mvā/svā heavy; pāda c syllables 5-7 da-nī-yā = ⏑ – – (pathyā) unchanged.

notes: The plant names are kept in Sanskrit. utkleśayanti (caus. of ut-√kliś) = stir up, excite (the noun utkleśa = nausea).

words.gram: n. nom. pl., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: गण्डीर, जलपिप्पली, तुम्बरु और शृङ्गवेरिका तीक्ष्ण, उष्ण, कटु और रूक्ष हैं तथा कफ और वात को हरने वाले हैं।
english: Gaṇḍīra, jalapippalī, tumbaru and śṛṅgaverikā are sharp, hot, pungent and dry, and remove Kapha and Vāta.
notes: Names kept in Sanskrit. jalapippalyaḥ is plural (the plant taken collectively). The neuter plural adjectives cover the mixed-gender group.

words.gram: f. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

words.gloss: removing disease and pain of the bladder

hindi: भूस्तृण पुंस्त्व का नाश करने वाला, कटु, रूक्ष और उष्ण तथा मुख का शोधन करने वाला है। खराह्वा कफ और वात का नाश करने वाली तथा बस्ति के रोग और पीड़ा को दूर करने वाली है।
english: Bhūstṛṇa destroys virility, is pungent, dry and hot, and cleanses the mouth. Kharāhvā destroys Kapha and Vāta and removes disease and pain of the bladder (basti).
notes: Names kept in Sanskrit. basti here = bladder. bhūstṛṇa is kept as one name (bhūs-tṛṇa 'earth-grass').

hindi: धान्यक, अजगन्धा और सुमुख — ये रुचिकारक, सुगन्धित और अधिक कटु नहीं हैं, तथा दोषों को उत्क्लिष्ट करते हैं।
english: Dhānyaka, ajagandhā and sumukha are appetizing, fragrant and not very pungent, and they stir up the doṣas.
notes: dhānyaka = coriander (standard); ajagandhā and sumukha kept in Sanskrit.

words.gloss: for arśas of Vāta and Kapha
words.gram: n. gen. pl., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: गृञ्जनक ग्राही और तीक्ष्ण है, वात और श्लेष्मा के अर्श में हितकर है; अपित्ती (व्यक्तियों) के लिए उसे स्वेदन और भोजन में प्रयुक्त करना चाहिए।
english: Gṛñjanaka is binding and sharp, wholesome in arśas of Vāta and Kapha; for those without Pitta (affliction) one should employ it in sweating and in eating.
notes: vātaśleṣmārśasām may also be the gen. pl. of arśasa 'one suffering from arśas' ('for those with Vāta-Kapha arśas'); the sense is the same. apittin = one who does not have (excess) Pitta. gṛñjanaka kept in Sanskrit.

hindi: पलाण्डु श्लेष्मा बढ़ाने वाला और मारुत का नाश करने वाला है, और पित्त को दूर करने वाला नहीं है; वह आहार में प्रयोग के योग्य, बलकारक, गुरु, वृष्य और रुचिकारक है।
english: Palāṇḍu increases Kapha (śleṣman) and destroys Vāta (māruta), and does not remove Pitta; it is suited for use in food, strengthening, heavy, aphrodisiac and appetizing.
notes: palāṇḍu = onion (standard).

words.gram: m. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: लशुन कृमि, कुष्ठ और किलास का नाश करने वाला, वात का नाश करने वाला, गुल्म को नष्ट करने वाला, स्निग्ध, उष्ण और वृष्य, कटु और गुरु है।
english: Laśuna destroys worms (krimi), kuṣṭha and kilāsa, destroys Vāta, destroys gulma, and is unctuous, hot and aphrodisiac, pungent and heavy.
notes: laśuna = garlic (standard). kuṣṭha, kilāsa and gulma kept in Sanskrit, no identifications.

words.gram: n. nom. pl., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: ये सूखे हुए, और इनके फल, कफ और वात का नाश करने वाले हैं। और हरितों का यह छठा वर्ग पूर्ण होता है।
english: These, when dried, and their fruits destroy Kapha and Vāta. And this sixth group, of the greens, is concluded.
notes: 'These' (etāni) refers to the items of the greens group. ayaṃ ... eṣaḥ are two demonstratives for the one group ('this, the sixth group').

hindi: अब मद्यवर्ग — सामान्यतः सब मद्य प्रकृति से अम्ल और उष्ण है, और विपाक में अम्ल कहा गया है; उसकी विशेषता बताई जाएगी।
english: Now the group of madya: in general all madya is by nature sour and hot, and is stated to be sour in vipāka (post-digestive effect); its particulars will be taught.
notes: The heading 'atha madyavargaḥ' is printed on the verse line but is outside the metre. madya (alcoholic drink) is kept as the Sanskrit word. viśeṣa is taken as 'particular features' (viśeṣa as a category is not meant here). sarvaṃ sāmānyataḥ may also close the statement ('all this in general'), with 'its particulars will be taught' following.
lines_deva: अथ मद्यवर्गः--- प्रकृत्या मद्यमम्लोष्णमम्लं चोक्तं विपाकतः
lines_iast: atha madyavargaḥ--- prakṛtyā madyamamloṣṇamamlaṃ coktaṃ vipākataḥ

words.gloss: for those whose urine is obstructed
for those with grahaṇī and arśas disorders
words.gram: m. gen. pl., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member, -in)

words.gloss: in loss of breast-milk and blood
words.gram: m. loc. pl., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: वात का नाश करने वाली सुरा कृश व्यक्तियों, रुके हुए मूत्र वालों, और ग्रहणी तथा अर्श के विकार वालों के लिए, और स्तन्य तथा रक्त के क्षय में प्रशस्त है।
english: Surā, which destroys Vāta, is recommended for the lean, for those whose urine is obstructed, for those with grahaṇī and arśas disorders, and in loss of breast-milk (stanya) and of blood.
notes: surā and the disease names grahaṇī and arśas kept in Sanskrit.

words.gloss: in hiccup, dyspnoea, coryza, cough, retention of faeces and loss of taste
words.gram: f. loc. sg., samāhāra dvandva (feminine of the last member aruci, as printed)

hindi: वात का नाश करने वाली मदिरा हिक्का, श्वास, प्रतिश्याय, कास, मल के रुकने और अरुचि में, तथा वमन, आनाह और विबन्ध में हितकर है।
english: Madirā, which destroys Vāta, is wholesome in hiccup (hikkā), dyspnoea (śvāsa), coryza (pratiśyāya), cough, retention of faeces and loss of taste (aruci), and in vomiting, distension (ānāha) and constipation (vibandha).
notes: The first compound ends in the loc. sg. of aruci (f.), a samāhāra dvandva that keeps the feminine gender of its last member (aruci) instead of the usual neuter; kept as printed, no flag. madirā kept in Sanskrit.

words.gloss: for pain, pravāhikā, āṭopa and arśas of Kapha and Vāta
words.gram: n. gen. pl., dvandva (last member a tat-puruṣa)

hindi: जगल शूल, प्रवाहिका, आटोप और कफ तथा वात के अर्श में हितकर है; वह ग्राही, रूक्ष और उष्ण, शोफ का नाश करने वाला और भोजन को पचाने वाला है।
english: Jagala is wholesome for pain, pravāhikā, āṭopa (rumbling) and arśas of Kapha and Vāta; it is binding, dry and hot, removes swelling and digests food.
notes: pravāhikā (lit. 'straining') and āṭopa (lit. 'puffing up', rumbling of the bowels) kept in Sanskrit with a literal gloss, no identifications. jagala kept in Sanskrit.

words.gloss: śoṣa, arśas, grahaṇī disorder, pāṇḍu disease, loss of taste and fevers

hindi: रुचिकारक और दीपन अरिष्ट शोष, अर्श, ग्रहणीदोष, पाण्डुरोग, अरुचि और ज्वर का तथा कफ से उत्पन्न रोगों का नाश करता है।
english: Ariṣṭa, appetizing and stimulating digestion, destroys śoṣa (wasting), arśas, grahaṇī disorder (grahaṇīdoṣa), pāṇḍu disease, loss of taste and fever, and diseases caused by Kapha.
notes: doṣa in grahaṇīdoṣa = disorder (of grahaṇī). śoṣa kept in Sanskrit with a literal gloss. 'And' before 'diseases caused by Kapha' is understood (no ca in the line).

hindi: शार्कर मुख को प्रिय, सुखद मद वाला, सुगन्धित, बस्तिरोग को दूर करने वाला है; पका हुआ (होने पर) वह पाचन कराने वाला, हृद्य और वर्ण्य है।
english: Śārkara is pleasing to the mouth, gives a pleasant mada (intoxication), is fragrant and removes bladder (basti) disease; when matured (pariṇata), it promotes digestion (jaraṇīya), and it is pleasing to the heart and good for the complexion.
notes: śārkara is a derived word ('of śarkarā'); kept in Sanskrit. mada kept as the Sanskrit word. jaraṇīya (-anīya of √jṝ) is taken in the active sense 'promoting digestion', like the -anīya group names (jīvanīya, bṛṃhaṇīya) and beside dīpana in 191; 'easily digested' is possible. pariṇata 'matured' is taken as 'when aged'.

words.gloss: destroying disorders of sneha and Kapha

hindi: पक्वरस रुचिकारक, दीपन, हृद्य, शोष, शोफ और अर्श में हितकर, स्नेह और श्लेष्मा के विकारों का नाश करने वाला और वर्ण्य माना गया है।
english: Pakvarasa is held to be appetizing, stimulating digestion, pleasing to the heart, wholesome for śoṣa, swelling and arśas, destructive of disorders of sneha (unctuous substance) and Kapha (śleṣman), and good for the complexion.
notes: pakvarasa (a madya made from cooked juice) kept in Sanskrit.

words.gram: m. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: शीतरसिक पाचन कराने वाला, विबन्ध का नाश करने वाला, स्वर और वर्ण का शोधन करने वाला, लेखन, और शोफ, उदर तथा अर्श में हितकर है।
english: Śītarasika promotes digestion (jaraṇīya), destroys constipation (vibandha), clears the voice and complexion, is reducing (lekhana), and is wholesome for swelling, udara and arśas.
notes: śītarasika ('of cold, i.e. uncooked, juice') is a derived name, not split; kept in Sanskrit. jaraṇīya as in 183. udara and arśas kept in Sanskrit.

words.gloss: by which faeces and wind are released and broken up
wholesome in pāṇḍu disease and wounds
words.gram: f. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: गौड मल और वायु को निकालने तथा भेदने वाला, तर्पण और दीपन है। आक्षिकी पाण्डुरोग और व्रण में हितकर तथा दीपनी मानी गई है।
english: Gauḍa releases and breaks up faeces and wind, and is replenishing (tarpaṇa) and stimulates digestion. Ākṣikī is held to be wholesome in pāṇḍu disease and wounds (vraṇa), and to stimulate digestion.
notes: gauḍa ('of guḍa') and ākṣikī are madyas, kept in Sanskrit; ākṣikī here stands alone inside the madya group (178-195) and is taken as a madya (f., with dīpanī and matā); whether it is made from the ākṣikī fruit of 163 is not stated. Which of sṛṣṭa/bhinna goes with faeces and which with wind is not stated; both are kept together. vāta released from the body = wind.

hindi: सुरासव तीव्र मद वाला, वात का नाश करने वाला और मुख को प्रिय है। मध्वासव छेदी और तीक्ष्ण है; मैरेय मधुर और गुरु है।
english: Surāsava has intense mada, destroys Vāta and is pleasing to the mouth. Madhvāsava is cutting (chedin) and sharp; maireya is sweet and heavy.
notes: surāsava, madhvāsava and maireya kept in Sanskrit; mada kept as the Sanskrit word.

words.gloss: āsava of mṛdvīkā and sugarcane juice
words.gram: m. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: धातकी से अभिषुत, मृद्वीका और ईख के रस का आसव हृद्य, रूक्ष, रुचिकारक और दीपन है; (वह) माध्वीक के समान है और अधिक उष्ण नहीं है।
english: The āsava of mṛdvīkā and sugarcane juice, fermented with dhātakī, is pleasing to the heart, dry, appetizing and stimulating digestion; it is like mādhvīka, and not very hot.
notes: SENTENCE: line a has no noun of its own and is taken with the subject of line b (mṛdvīkekṣurasāsavaḥ); it could also be a separate item ('that fermented with dhātakī'). mādhvīkavat is taken as its own predicate, joined by 'na ca' to 'not very hot'. mṛdvīkā = grape (standard); dhātakī and mādhvīka kept in Sanskrit. abhiṣuta (abhi-√su 'pressed out, fermented') taken as 'fermented'.

hindi: मधु रुचिकारक, दीपन, हृद्य, बलकारक और पित्त का अविरोधी है, तथा विबन्ध का नाश करने वाला, कफ का नाश करने वाला, लघु और अल्प मारुत (करने) वाला है।
english: Madhu is appetizing, stimulates digestion, is pleasing to the heart, strengthening and not opposed to Pitta; it destroys constipation and Kapha, is light and (causes) little Vāta (māruta).
notes: madhu stands inside the madya group (178-195), so it is taken as a drink named madhu, not honey; kept in Sanskrit. alpamāruta (bahuvrīhi 'having little māruta') is taken as 'causing little Vāta'.
lines_deva: रोचनं दीपनं हृद्यं बल्यं पित्ताविरोधि च
lines_iast: rocanaṃ dīpanaṃ hṛdyaṃ balyaṃ pittāvirodhi ca

words.gram: f. nom. sg., -la derivative of the dvandva vāta-pitta

hindi: जौ की सुरा मण्ड सहित रूक्ष और उष्ण, वात और पित्त बढ़ाने वाली, गुरु है और विष्टम्भ करके पचती है; किन्तु मधूलिका श्लेष्मा बढ़ाने वाली है।
english: Surā of barley, with its maṇḍa, is dry and hot, increases Vāta and Pitta, is heavy and is digested after causing obstruction (viṣṭambha); but madhūlikā increases Kapha (śleṣman).
notes: gurvī jīryati viṣṭabhya is taken with the barley surā (the clause of madhūlikā begins with 'śleṣmalā tu'); it could also describe madhūlikā. maṇḍa and madhūlikā kept in Sanskrit.
lines_deva: गुर्वी जीर्यति विष्टभ्य श्लेष्मला तु मधूलिका
lines_iast: gurvī jīryati viṣṭabhya śleṣmalā tu madhūlikā

words.gloss: removing diseases of the heart, pāṇḍu and worms
words.gram: n. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)
n. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: सौवीरक और तुषोदक दीपन और पाचन कराने वाले, हृदय, पाण्डु और कृमि के रोगों को दूर करने वाले, ग्रहणी और अर्श में हितकर और भेदी हैं।
english: Sauvīraka and tuṣodaka stimulate digestion and promote digestion (jaraṇīya), remove diseases of the heart, pāṇḍu and worms (krimi), are wholesome in grahaṇī and arśas, and are breaking (purgative).
notes: sauvīraka and tuṣodaka (lit. 'husk-water') kept in Sanskrit; the singular neuter adjectives agree with the samāhāra dvandva. tuṣodaka is kept as one name. jaraṇīya as in 183.

words.gram: n. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)
n. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: अम्ल काञ्जिक स्पर्श से दाह और ज्वर को दूर करने वाला, पीने से वात और कफ को दूर करने वाला, विबन्ध का नाश करने वाला, अवस्रंसी और दीपन है।
english: Sour kāñjika removes burning and fever by touch, removes Vāta and Kapha by drinking, destroys constipation (vibandha), is laxative (avasraṃsin) and stimulates digestion.
notes: kāñjika kept in Sanskrit. dāhajvara may also be one disease ('burning fever'); taken as a dvandva.

words.gram: n. nom. sg., karmadhāraya of guru and tat-puruṣa

hindi: प्रायः नया मद्य गुरु और दोषों को प्रेरित करने वाला है; पुराना (मद्य) स्रोतों का शोधन करने वाला, दीपन, लघु और रुचिकारक है।
english: Generally, new madya is heavy and stirs up the doṣas; old (madya) cleanses the channels (srotas), stimulates digestion, and is light and appetizing.
notes: samīraṇa here = setting in motion (of the doṣas), not Vāta. guru may also be read as a separate word; the sense is the same.
lines_deva: स्रोतसां शोधनं जीर्णं दीपनं लघु रोचनम्
lines_iast: srotasāṃ śodhanaṃ jīrṇaṃ dīpanaṃ laghu rocanam

words.gram: n. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

words.gloss: giving boldness, vigour, intelligence, contentment, nourishment and strength
words.gram: n. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: मद्य हर्ष देने वाला, प्रीणन, भय, शोक और श्रम को दूर करने वाला, तथा प्रगल्भता, वीर्य, प्रतिभा, तुष्टि, पुष्टि और बल देने वाला है।
english: Madya is exhilarating and gladdening, removes fear, grief and fatigue (śrama), and gives boldness, vigour, intelligence (pratibhā), contentment, nourishment and strength.

text_flags.why: grammar: '-rpadam' is no Sanskrit form; the list of things given needs -pradam 'giving', parallel to -apaham in line a (र्प for प्र, transposed letters). Metre does not decide: 16 syllables either way and ba-lar-pa-dam / ba-la-pra-dam both scan ⏑ – ⏑ – (la heavy before pr), so pāda d syllables 5-7 = ⏑ – ⏑ (pathyā) in both.

notes: pratibhā 'intelligence, quick wit' kept with the Sanskrit word.

hindi: सात्त्विक (जनों) द्वारा विधिपूर्वक और युक्ति से पिया गया (मद्य) अमृत के समान होगा। मद्य को लेकर यह सातवाँ वर्ग कहा गया।
english: Drunk by sāttvika (persons) according to rule and with rational planning (yukti), (madya) would be like amṛta (nectar). This seventh group has been declared with regard to madya.
notes: sāttvika = those in whom sattva (the mind's clear quality) predominates.

words.gloss: from the surface of the sky

hindi: अब जलवर्ग — सब जल एक प्रकार का है; वह ऐन्द्र (जल के रूप में) आकाशतल से गिरता है। गिरता हुआ और गिरा हुआ वह देश और काल की अपेक्षा रखता है।
english: Now the group of waters: all water is of one kind; it falls from the surface of the sky as Indra's (water). Falling and fallen, it depends on place and time.
notes: The heading 'atha jalavargaḥ' is printed on the verse line but is outside the metre. aindra 'belonging to Indra' = the water of rain.
lines_deva: अथ जलवर्गः--- जलमेकविधं सर्वं पतत्यैन्द्रं नभस्तलात्
lines_iast: atha jalavargaḥ--- jalamekavidhaṃ sarvaṃ patatyaindraṃ nabhastalāt

words.gloss: by soma, air and the sun
cold, hot, unctuous, dry and the rest
words.gram: m. inst. pl., bahuvrīhi (dvandva first member)

words.gloss: by the qualities of the earth

hindi: आकाश से गिरता हुआ (जल) काल का अनुसरण करने वाले सोम, वायु और सूर्य से, और जैसा समीप हो वैसे, शीत, उष्ण, स्निग्ध, रूक्ष आदि पृथ्वी के गुणों से स्पृष्ट होता है।
english: Falling from the sky, (water) is touched by soma, air and the sun, which follow the season (kāla), and, according to what is near, by the qualities of the earth, cold, hot, unctuous, dry and the rest.

text_flags.why: 'śota' is no Sanskrit word; the line's list runs in opposed pairs (śīta/uṣṇa, snigdha/rūkṣa), which needs śīta 'cold' (शो for शी). Metre neutral: 16 syllables, śo and śī both heavy by the long vowel; pāda c syllables 5-7 dha-rū-kṣā = ⏑ – – (pathyā) unchanged.

notes: vāyu with soma and the sun (arka) is taken as the element air. kāla may mean time or season; 'season' is given. yathāsanna 'according to what is near' is taken with mahīguṇaiḥ (the qualities of the earth it comes near).

hindi: प्रकृति से दिव्य जल शीत, शुचि, शिव, मृष्ट, निर्मल और लघु — छह गुणों वाला है; गिर जाने पर वह पात्र की अपेक्षा रखता है।
english: By nature heavenly water is cold, pure, wholesome, clean (mṛṣṭa), clear and light, having six qualities; once fallen, it depends on the receptacle.
notes: mṛṣṭa may mean 'clean' or 'pleasant-tasting'; 'clean' is given. pātra 'receptacle' is the ground on which it falls (see 199).
lines_deva: शीतं शुचि शिवं मृष्टं विमलं लघु षड्गुणम्
lines_iast: śītaṃ śuci śivaṃ mṛṣṭaṃ vimalaṃ laghu ṣaḍguṇam

words.gram: n. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa, ppp. sam-√sṛj
n. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa, ppp. anu-√i

hindi: श्वेत (भूमि) पर (जल) कषाय होता है, पाण्डुर पर तो तिक्त होता है, कपिल पर क्षार से मिला हुआ और ऊषर पर लवणयुक्त होता है।
english: On white (ground) it becomes astringent, but on pale (ground) bitter, on tawny (ground) mixed with alkali (kṣāra), and on saline ground (ūṣara) salty.
notes: The ground is understood (the receptacle of 198); the noun is not printed. kaṣāya here is the taste, astringent. The sentence may continue into the next unit.
lines_deva: श्वेते कषायं भवति पाण्डरे स्यात्तु तिक्तकम्
lines_iast: śvete kaṣāyaṃ bhavati pāṇḍare syāttu tiktakam
